exact_claim: Arnold's five metrical strata are chronological stages of composition.
attested_or_hypothetical: Hypothetical framework over an attested corpus. The corpus is attested; the periodisation is a 1905 interpretation.
chronological_fit: CANNOT BE CHECKED. The framework is the chronology under test; there is no external date to fit it to (DA-D-001).
geographical_fit: Not applicable — the claim is about time, not place.
contact_mechanism: Mechanism required: that metrical style changed monotonically over the composition period and that Arnold's features track that change. Neither is evidenced in this record.
positive_evidence: Grassmann 1876-7 flags stanzas that sit in Arnold's late strata at 2.34 times the base rate within books 1-9, i.e. with book 10 removed (DA-M-012) - SUBJECT TO DA-M-023: whether Arnold 1905 used Grassmann 1876-7 is untested and untestable here (DEP-036), so this is not established as INDEPENDENT support. Book 10 is 74.79% Arnold-late and is separately singled out by SRC-105's cluster analysis (DA-005).
contrary_evidence: Book order and stratum do not co-vary, though at n=10 that excludes nothing (DA-M-003). Three books contain no Archaic pada and two contain no Cretic pada (DA-M-005). Metre label and stratum are strongly associated, Cramer's V = 0.5314 (DA-M-006, DA-016). Sixteen keys in the companion apparatus name stanzas that strata.json does not divide (DA-M-022). SRC-105 reports a null for allomorphic support of the proposed stratifications, and whether Arnold's is inside 'any of the proposed stratifications' is UNDETERMINED (DA-008).
independent_support: ONE instrument: Grassmann. Oldenberg and Wuest are one instrument between them (DEP-030); Arnold(Sketch) is Arnold (DEP-035); Witzel overlaps both at ~0.48.
source_dependencies: DEP-001, DEP-004, DEP-006, DEP-022, DEP-029, DEP-030, DEP-031, DEP-035. The framework itself is single-sourced to Arnold 1905, which could not be reopened (SRC-100).
current_specialist_standing: DISPUTED and actively re-tested. SRC-105 (2021, JAOS, 5 citations at retrieval) reviews previous stratifications and reports no significant allomorphic support. Scite, the instrument that would measure how that has been received, refused for quota (SRC-104).
diagnostic_predictions: If chronological: a non-metrical, non-Arnold instrument should separate the strata after controlling for metrical genre; the separation should not vanish when book 10 is removed; and strata should not be wholly absent from whole books.
falsifier: A study showing that Arnold's stratum assignment is predicted by metrical genre and content alone, with no residual time signal, once book is controlled. SRC-105 may already be that study; the abstract does not say, and the full text is not retrieved.
eligible_for_extended_analysis: NO — but not because it failed. It cannot be gated while its own source is unreadable.
proportional_space: A named framework under audit, cited with its dependency, never as a period label.
reason: Arnold 1905 is EGRESS_BLOCKED (SRC-100) and the Hellwig, Scarlata and Widmer full text is unretrieved (SRC-105). The two documents that would decide this are both unreadable in this session. Gating on the abstracts alone would be exactly the failure the inheritance rule forbids.

exact_claim: Mandala number tracks time: lower-numbered family books are earlier.
attested_or_hypothetical: Hypothetical. The arrangement is attested; that it is chronological is a proposal.
chronological_fit: CANNOT BE TESTED AT THIS SIZE. rho = -0.0667 at an exact two-sided permutation p of 0.8651; the null 95% range of rho at n=10 runs to +0.636 (DA-M-003, table A11).
contact_mechanism: Would require that the compilers ordered by age and that their ordering survived. Neither is evidenced here; the compilation date itself is unestablished (DA-D-003).
positive_evidence: Book 10's late share (74.79%) is far above every other book, which is consistent with 10 being last. Nothing else in the measured set supports an ordering.
contrary_evidence: Books 8 and 9 carry the lowest Arnold-late shares in the corpus and books 5, 6 and 7 sit within three points of book 1 (DA-M-004); 23 of 45 book pairs are inverted (DA-M-003). None of this is significant at n=10.
independent_support: None retrieved. SRC-105's abstract reports between-book differences 'not substantial' apart from book 10, which if anything cuts against.
source_dependencies: DEP-004 records that the by-book instrument and the Arnold instrument are entangled at the late end and are not two measures.
current_specialist_standing: The family-book grouping itself is standard; the claim that its NUMBERING is chronological is much weaker and is not supported by anything retrieved here.
diagnostic_predictions: If true, an instrument independent of both metre and book should order 2 < 3 < 4 < 5 < 6 < 7 monotonically.
falsifier: Not met, and not meetable on ten units. An instrument with more than ten orderable units - hymn-level or pada-level rather than book-level - could test it.
proportional_space: One sentence wherever a book number is used, stating that the number is an arrangement fact and that whether it tracks time is untested here.
reason: REPAIRED 2026-09-09 after adversarial review. This row previously read NOT-ELIGIBLE with the reason 'FAILS on the one instrument this repository can run'. That was wrong twice over. First, the test is underpowered: p = 0.8651 excludes nothing. Second, it is inconsistent with DA-003, which refuses to draw the POSITIVE inference from the same instrument on the ground that a metrical instrument ranking book 9 earliest is probably reporting book 9's metres; an instrument that cannot license the positive inference cannot license the exclusion either. The book-order hypothesis is a standard scholarly position and this unit does not gate it out. It is UNTESTED here, which is a different verdict from failed. What survives is the method rule at DA-003: family-book location is an attestation fact and the number is not a date - held because the two are different claims, not because the second was refuted.

exact_claim: The transmitted Rigveda is a phonetically faithful record of the composed hymns.
attested_or_hypothetical: Hypothetical, and testable directly against the bundle.
positive_evidence: Accent and syllable count survive well enough for a metrical restoration to be attempted at all, and for a word-analysis to align to the recited text at ~91% of segments (DA-012).
contrary_evidence: DECISIVE. 72.04% of stanzas differ between the transmitted and the metrically restored text (DA-M-015); the recited text is recoverable letter-for-letter from the padapatha in 22 of 10,552 stanzas (DA-M-018).
independent_support: Not required; the corpus refutes it internally.
source_dependencies: SRC-078 is an editorial reconstruction, so the 72.04% is a difference from van Nooten and Holland's judgement, not from a manuscript.
current_specialist_standing: Not a scholarly position; it is the popular framing constitution 4.A names as a trap.
diagnostic_predictions: If true, no metrical restoration would be needed and the padapatha would be a segmentation.
proportional_space: A concise exclusion with the two numbers attached. Not a section.
reason: Refuted by measurement over the pinned corpus (DA-009). Method step 7: failure means a concise exclusion, not an equal section.

exact_claim: Panini's grammar reshaped the transmitted Rigvedic text.
chronological_fit: CANNOT-GATE. Panini's own date is not established in this repository (DA-D-006) and neither is the Samhitapatha fixation date (DA-D-004), so the two cannot be ordered.
contact_mechanism: Would require a route by which a descriptive grammar altered a recitational tradition. Not investigated here.
contrary_evidence: None retrieved. The absence on BOTH sides is the finding.
independent_support: None. No Panini source exists in 02-SOURCES/access-ledger.csv.
source_dependencies: None, because nothing has been retrieved.
diagnostic_predictions: Not formulable without reading a chandasi rule.
reason: Zero retrieval. Constitution 4.A asks what the chandasi rules imply and this repository has never opened Panini. Typed NOT PRODUCED under the negative-evidence standard: no search for a Panini source has been run in any session, so the absence is a fact about this record and carries no evidential weight whatever. HOLD-008.

exact_claim: The conventional composition date of roughly 1500-1200 BCE is established by the four standard arguments.
attested_or_hypothetical: Hypothetical, and inferred at every step. No attestation exists (DA-D-001).
chronological_fit: The pillars do not compose into a point. Retrieved positions span c.1750-1000 BCE for the Iranian anchor alone (DA-C-004).
geographical_fit: Pillar 2 is anchored in northern Mesopotamia and pillar 3's retrieved comparison chronology is Near Eastern (SRC-113), neither of which is where the Rigveda is placed.
contact_mechanism: Pillar 1 requires an unstated rate of linguistic divergence; no retrieved source supplies one (DA-C-001).
positive_evidence: Parpola 2015 ch.9 states c.1300-1200 BCE for the Rigveda on named grounds (SRC-106). Elby 2014 reports Proferes' Brahmana date of roughly 1100 BCE (SRC-114).
contrary_evidence: The three retrieved readings of the Mitanni evidence are mutually incompatible, 1909-2015 (DA-C-002). The absence-of-iron premise has been contested since 1915 (SRC-116) and the same argument form is run in a retrieved source to a date 1,300 years earlier (SRC-115).
independent_support: None of the five pillars reaches a year without another (DA-C-007).
source_dependencies: DEP-033 (the Brahmana anchor is single-sourced through one survey citing one book); DEP-034 (all connector returns are one lane's worth); SRC-095 and SRC-100 (no DOI dereferenceable, no abstract checkable against its publisher).
current_specialist_standing: The RANGE is standard. The point estimate is not, and the retrieved sources that state a figure state different ones.
diagnostic_predictions: A dated inscription, a dated South Asian iron horizon read against a settled reading of ayas-, or an independently dated Gathic corpus would each move it.
falsifier: Any dated external attestation of a Rigvedic hymn. None exists.
eligible_for_extended_analysis: YES, as a range and as historiography.
proportional_space: Proportional to the evidence, which is thin and inferential. The range is written as a range and the inference chain is shown.
reason: It clears the gate as a RANGE supported by named sources, and only as a range. It does not clear it as a point estimate, and DA-C-006 states the range this record can defend rather than a figure.
